title: Using kan, vil, må, and skal
goal: Build simple sentences with kan, vil, må, and skal plus a bare infinitive.

objectives.statement: Build simple sentences with kan, vil, må, and skal plus a bare infinitive.

spans.value: It is Saturday morning. Nora and Amir share a flat in Oslo. They are deciding what to do before Nora’s sister visits in the afternoon.
Hva skal du gjøre i dag?

blocks.translation: What are you going to do today?

spans.value: Ja, men jeg må gå nå. Butikken stenger tidlig.

blocks.translation: Yes, but I have to leave now. The shop closes early.

spans.value: Vent litt. Jeg vil lage suppe, så vi må kjøpe grønnsaker.

blocks.translation: Wait a moment. I want to make soup, so we have to buy vegetables.

spans.value: Greit. Skal vi spise hjemme i kveld?

blocks.translation: All right. Shall we eat at home this evening?

spans.value: Ja. Søsteren min kan komme klokka seks.

blocks.translation: Yes. My sister can come at six.

spans.value: Da skal jeg kjøpe litt ekstra mat.

blocks.translation: Then I’ll buy some extra food.

spans.value: You already know that Norwegian often uses the infinitive marker

The form of the modal verb does not change with the subject:
The main decision is therefore not which ending to use. It is which meaning you want: ability or possibility, desire, necessity, or a plan.
when someone is able to do something or when something is possible.

en.value: I can speak a little Norwegian.

spans.value: describes what a person is able to do.

no.value: Søsteren min kan komme klokka seks.

spans.value: presents six o’clock as possible. Compare:

en.value: She is going to come today.

spans.value: The first sentence says that coming today is possible. The second presents it as her plan.

spans.value: with a bare infinitive to present an intended or arranged action. English often uses “am/is/are going to” in the translation.

en.value: I’m going to meet Eva at three.

spans.value: These sentences do not describe four different actions. They show four different ways of viewing the same action:

items.value: presents a plan or intended action.

en.value: They are going to travel tomorrow.
They are going to travel tomorrow.

spans.value: The shared grammar pattern is easy to see, but choosing the correct modal requires attention to the situation.
Imagine that Jonas is talking about a concert:

en.value: Jonas can go to the concert.
Jonas wants to go to the concert.
Jonas has to go to the concert.
Jonas is going to go to the concert.

items.value: Which bare infinitive names the action?

spans.value: Amir is now ready to leave. Nora checks the plan one more time.
Ja, det kan jeg. Hva vil du spise til dessert?

blocks.translation: Yes, I can. What do you want to eat for dessert?

spans.value: Jeg vil lage eplekake, men jeg må kjøpe epler.

blocks.translation: I want to make apple cake, but I have to buy apples.

spans.value: Greit. Jeg skal kjøpe epler også.

blocks.translation: All right. I’ll buy apples too.

spans.value: Flott. Da kan vi spise eplekake i kveld.

blocks.translation: Great. Then we can eat apple cake this evening.

items.value: Nora asks about Amir’s ability with
Nora presents a future possibility with

spans.value: All five combinations use a bare infinitive.
The most important form mistake is placing
between the modal and the action verb.
Changing the modal for the subject
Do not add a special ending because the subject changes.
Choosing by action rather than meaning
No action verb automatically belongs with one modal.

en.value: I am going to eat now.

spans.value: Choose the modal from the intended meaning, not from the action itself.

sections.title: Transfer: preparing for a day trip

spans.value: Now change the situation. Lea and Henrik are preparing for a Sunday trip to the forest. They have a plan, but they also have practical needs and personal wishes.

Lea is able to drive. Henrik wants to take photographs. They have to leave before nine. They are going to meet their friend Mari at the station. Later, good weather may make an outdoor lunch possible.

Without looking back, write one short sentence of 3–12 words in a new situation. A friend asks what you want to do on a bird-watching walk. You enjoy taking photographs, and no task or fixed plan has been set. State your preference with a modal followed directly by the action verb, without

prompt.value: Complete the sentences with the correct form of the verb after the modal verb.

explanation.value: Etter «kan», «vil», «må» og «skal» bruker vi infinitiv uten «å».

prompt.value: Put together the sentence that tells about an ability.
Put together the sentence that tells what Mina wants.
Choose the pair that fits the dialogues, in the correct order.

options.text: Nora må gå hjem. Nora vil gå hjem.
options.why: This reverses the intended meanings of the two situations.

options.text: Nora vil gå hjem. Nora må gå hjem.
options.why: The first sentence expresses desire, while the second expresses necessity.

text.value: «Jeg har lyst til å gå hjem, men jeg trenger ikke.»
«Så du blir litt til?»
«Ja, gjerne.»
«Jeg er nødt til å gå hjem nå.»
«Hvorfor det?»
«Den siste bussen går snart.»

prompt.value: Put together the sentence that tells about the arrangement.
Choose the option that fits all four facts about Jonas, in the correct order.

options.text: Jonas må å dekke bordet. Jonas skal å handle i kveld. Jonas kan å bake brød. Jonas vil å lage suppe.
options.why: The meanings match, but å is incorrectly placed after every modal.

options.text: Jonas skal dekke bordet. Jonas må handle i kveld. Jonas vil bake brød. Jonas kan lage suppe.
options.why: The sentences use bare infinitives, but the modal meanings are in the wrong order.

options.text: Jonas må dekke bordet. Jonas skal handle i kveld. Jonas kan bake brød. Jonas vil lage suppe.
options.why: The modals express necessity, an arranged plan, ability, and desire in the order given.

stem.value: Choose the option with the correct meaning and form in every sentence.

text.value: «Er Jonas nødt til å dekke bordet før gjestene kommer?»
«Ja, det er nødvendig.»
«Er det avtalt at han handler i kveld?»
«Ja, det er avtalt.»
«Har han lært seg å bake brød?»
«Ja, han har lært det.»
«Har han lyst til å lage suppe?»
«Ja, det har han lyst til.»

prompt.value: Put together one sentence for each line, in the same order.

text.value: «Jeg har lyst til å lage suppe.»
«Vi har ingen grønnsaker, så jeg er nødt til å kjøpe dem.»
«Det er avtalt at jeg handler litt ekstra i dag.»
«Jeg har mulighet til å spise hjemme i kveld.»

«Jeg er flink til å kjøre, så det går fint.»

«Vi er nødt til å dra før klokka ni.»

prompt.value: Write that you want to take photos on the trip. Use a modal verb with an infinitive without «å».

payload.judge_prompt: Evaluate preference, modal-choice, bare-infinitive as gating criteria. The response must be one short Norwegian sentence that states the speaker wants to take photographs on the walk, using «vil» directly followed by a bare infinitive. Accept natural alternatives such as «Jeg vil fotografere», «Jeg vil fotografere fuglene», and «Jeg vil ta bilder av fuglene». Anchor that must pass: «Jeg vil ta bilder av fuglene.»

criteria.instruction: States that the speaker wants or prefers to take photographs during the walk, rather than merely being able, required, or scheduled to do so.
Uses «vil» to express this personal desire; accept natural variations in wording and the activity phrase.
Places the bare infinitive directly after «vil», with no «å» between them.
